problem: LAMBDA-HOLD. The paper argues that RL on muscle-level action spaces explores inefficiently for two reasons. First, independent per-muscle excitation noise largely cancels in the many-to-one excitation-to-joint map. Second, the policy must emit a full excitation vector 'hundreds of times per second' (p.2, sections 1.2-1.3). It groups prior remedies into fixed reflex rules with tuned gains, correlated noise (OU/pink/gSDE), DEP-RL, and fixed synergy bases, and says all of them impose coordination from outside (pp.2-3, section 1.4). Lambda-Hold changes the control variable to per-muscle equilibrium-point threshold lengths (lambda). A fixed stretch-reflex law turns lambda into excitations, and lambda is held between gait events. The paper claims 'to our knowledge, the first coordinated, human-like sprinting' in predictive musculoskeletal simulation from a forward-velocity reward alone (p.3, section 1.5). KINESIS. The paper says torque humanoids miss joint constraints and overactuated muscle control, and that muscle-driven locomotion work is narrow or lacks comparison with human data (p.1). Kinesis trains a model-free PPO motion-imitation policy on 1.8 h of KIT locomotion (walk, gradual turn, turn in place, walk backwards, short runs) for MyoLeg variants with 80, 86 and 290 muscles. It reuses the result as a locomotion prior for downstream tasks and compares its muscle patterns with EMG (pp.1-2). FOR THIS PROGRAMME the question is whether either method can supply an unassisted MuJoCo sprinting human that meets the replication gate: median maximum speed >= 4.0 m/s over 5 seeds, with the published reward unchanged and no increase in muscle strength or shortening velocity.
mechanism_exact: LAMBDA-HOLD, from the paper unless marked. PLANT: H2190, a 3D model with 21 mechanical DOFs and 90 musculotendon units, simulated in SCONE with the Hyfydy engine. The simulation step is 0.01 s and every method shares it. At each step the engine exposes each muscle's length l_i and velocity v_i and takes excitation e_i in [0,1]. Both l_i and v_i are normalised by optimal fibre length, which is Hyfydy's default output format. Activation follows from e_i through the engine's activation dynamics, and force from activation plus force-length and force-velocity (p.3 section 2.1; p.4). RECRUITMENT LAW (Eq. 1, p.4): e_i = clip_[0,1]( G_tonic*(l_i - lambda_i) + G_phasic*max(v_i, 0) ). G_tonic = 50 and G_phasic = 0.1 are shared by all 90 muscles and fixed throughout; lambda_i is the policy command, bounded to [0.6, 1.2]. The tonic term is length feedback about the threshold (static stretch reflex). The phasic term is rectified velocity feedback (dynamic stretch reflex), so it only adds drive while the muscle is stretching. No neural delay appears anywhere. The law contains no coupling term; coordination comes from mechanically coupled lengths (p.4). HOLD: the policy emits lambda only at decision points and holds it until the next one, while the law keeps producing e from the evolving l and v at every 0.01 s step. The reward is accumulated over the hold. Each hold is one SAC transition, so exploration noise perturbs lambda once per decision and stays constant across the interval (pp.4 and 6). The paper stresses that this is not action repeat because the excitation keeps varying through the reflex loop (p.4). DECISION TIMING (p.4 section 2.3; Fig. 2 p.5): a decision fires whenever either foot changes contact state, i.e. when that foot's vertical GRF crosses 0.05 body weight rising (strike) or falling (toe-off). One sub-point is inserted between consecutive events at t_last_event + 0.5*T_est, where T_est is the gap between the third- and second-most-recent events. That gap is the most recent interval of the same type, because stance and flight intervals alternate. Every hold is bounded to [0.05, 0.15] s. Fixed-interval triggering was rejected because 'in our experience the stride period then settles at multiples of the hold' (p.4), which is anecdotal and not shown. Lambda is therefore updated 'only eight times per gait cycle' (p.12): four GRF events plus four sub-points per stride. LEARNING (p.5 section 2.4; Table 1 p.18): SAC with gSDE on Stable-Baselines3. Actor and critic are MLPs with two hidden layers of 256. gSDE noise is resampled every 4 decision steps. Learning rate 3e-4, gamma 0.99, target smoothing tau 0.005, batch 256, replay 5e5, 2 gradient steps per train_freq 1, entropy coefficient 'auto', 24 parallel environments, online mean/variance normalisation of observations and rewards. OBSERVATION (p.6): 432 dims covering muscle length and velocity (spindle Ia/II), MTU force (Golgi Ib), foot contact and GRF, joint angles and angular velocities, vestibular signals, and an efference copy of the held lambda. Excitation and activation are excluded. [COMPUTED here: the per-muscle blocks l, v, F and lambda give 4 x 90 = 360. If joints means the 21 DOFs, angles plus velocities give 42. That leaves 30 dims for contact/GRF plus vestibular, which the paper does not itemise.] ACTION: 90-dim lambda in [0.6,1.2]; the mapping from the squashed SAC output is not stated. REWARD (Eq. 2, p.6): r = exp(v_x) * exp(-(v_z/sigma_lat)^2) per 0.01 s step, with sigma_lat = 0.1 m/s. v_x is forward and v_z mediolateral centre-of-mass velocity. The velocity term is uncapped, and the lateral factor lies in [0,1]. TERMINATION (p.6): centre-of-mass height < 0.5 m or head height < 0.9 m. START: standing (p.7 'accelerates from a standing start'; p.17 'default standing posture'). EXTENSIONS that are 'not part of the controller evaluated in the main text' (App. B, p.17): (a) RSI with a Go-Explore-style self-generated archive of the highest-return episodes; after a 3e6-decision-step warm-up, 'a fraction' of resets draw their initial state from it (p.18). (b) A vmax curriculum that holds 10 L_opt/s until 3e6 decision steps, then raises vmax in unit increments to 20 over the next 150e6 simulation steps, on top of RSI (p.19). BASELINES (p.6 section 2.6), all with the same task and model: Plain SAC on 90 excitations every step; Excitation-hold, which holds excitations between the same decision points without a reflex; DEP-RL, the previous study's DEP+MPO implementation with its step-counted quantities rescaled from 0.025 s to 0.01 s (time windows and delays x2.5, per-step rates /2.5, gamma -> gamma^(1/2.5)); Synergy, a 30-dim latent (10 NMF synergy coefficients per leg with one basis shared by both legs, plus 10 independent trunk excitations), with the basis taken from NMF of lambda-hold's own best rollouts and mirroring omitted. KINESIS. PLANT: MyoSuite MyoLeg in MuJoCo, in three variants (p.2 section III.A): Legs with 80 MTUs and the upper body 'a rigid volume with mass'; Legs+Abs with 86 (six abdominal muscles for basic postural control); Legs+Back with 290. Body dimensions 'closely match the mean human body shape of the SMPL model'. DATA (p.2 section III.B; p.5; App. p.9): KIT-Locomotion is 1054 AMASS/KIT sequences (1.8 h), split 946 train and 108 test, covering five skills. The run skill is described as 'the subject breaks into a short running stride'. Clips are downsampled from 100 to 30 fps, mapped from SMPL onto a 24-joint MuJoCo template skeleton, and IK is run at several frames per trajectory to give random start states (p.3). POMDP (p.3): the observation holds pelvis height, tilt and velocity; each joint's position, velocity, angular position and angular velocity; feet contact forces; and the target pose at t+1 (absolute and relative). N = 309, 363 and 453 for the three models. The action is M muscle signals. REWARD (Eqs. 1-4 p.3; Table II p.5): a weighted sum of r_pos = exp(-k_pos * sum_i ||p_i - p_hat_i||^2) over pelvis, knees, ankles and toes (plus head for Abs/Back), r_vel = exp(-k_vel * sum ||v_i - v_hat_i||^2), r_e = -||m||_1 - ||m||_2 and r_up = exp(-k_up(theta_f^2 + theta_s^2)). Values: k_pos 200, k_vel 5, k_up 3; w_pos 0.6, w_vel 0.2; w_e 0.1/0.2/0.2 and w_up 0.1/0.0/0.0 for Legs/Abs/Back. ACTUATION (pp.3-4): in PD mode the action is a desired next-step muscle length, F_i = F_peak*(k_p(a_i - l_i) - k_d v_i), converted to activation through m_i = (F_i - F_P(l_i)) / (F_L(l_i) F_V(v_i)) (Eq. 5). In direct mode m = (a+1)/2. The paper states that direct control trained faster and scored better, and it was used for Abs/Back and downstream tasks. EPISODES (p.4): random motion and start frame; terminate if any tracked keypoint is > 0.15 m from the reference, otherwise stop at clip end. POLICY (pp.4-5): each expert is a Gaussian MLP with layers [2048,1536,1024,1024,512,512] and SiLU, trained with PPO plus Lattice exploration. Hard negative mining trains a copy of the current expert on the motions it failed, and repeats; 3 experts sufficed. An MoE gating MLP [1024,512,256] with softmax chooses among the frozen experts. TRAINING (p.5): one A100 with 128 CPU threads, 128 envs, 51,200 samples per epoch, 10 PPO rounds, lr 5e-5, gamma 0.99, epsilon 0.2, tau (GAE) 0.95, Adam; simulation at 150 Hz and control at 30 Hz. CODE AT cddab3c, differing from or adding to the paper: (1) The PD helper uses kp = 5*F0 and kd = 0.1*kp, clips force to [-F0, 0], and ignores the cfg kp_scale/kd_scale (src/env/myolegs_env.py:529-540); Table II lists k_p = k_d = 1. (2) Target lengths map a in [-1,1] to [0, lengthrange_max] (myolegs_env.py:558-575). (3) The PD law is recomputed every physics substep within a 30 Hz hold (myolegs_env.py:296-320). (4) The released Legs imitation checkpoint is evaluated in PD mode (cfg/run/eval_run_legs.yaml:10), while legs_back trains in direct mode (cfg/run/train_run_legs_back.yaml:10). (5) Legs proprioception = root_height, root_tilt, local body pos/rot/vel/ang_vel and 4 feet_contacts; task inputs = diff_local_body_pos, diff_local_vel, local_ref_body_pos (cfg/run/train_run_legs.yaml). (6) Value lr is 3e-4 and policy gradient clip 25 (cfg/learning/im_mlp.yaml). CROSS-LINK: Kinesis Legs-PD is structurally a lambda-like length-target controller: the muscle pulls when longer than its target, and the target is held over a fixed 1/30 s interval. It differs from lambda-hold in three ways: it inverts force through the F-L-V curves instead of using a reflex excitation law, it holds on a fixed clock instead of GRF events, and it tracks a reference.
protocol: LAMBDA-HOLD. Task: sprint from a standing start under the Eq. 2 reward. Each method is trained under an identical simulation-step budget; the Fig. 3/7 axes run to about 150e6 simulation steps and about 15e6 decision steps for the hold methods. The mean over 2 random seeds is plotted with a min-max band (Fig. 3 p.8; Fig. 7 p.18). Two axes are reported: simulation steps (equal environment experience) and decision steps (policy queries) (p.7 section 2.7). EXPLORATION (p.7 section 2.8): 15 anatomical joint velocities (the 6 pelvis DOFs excluded). (a) Kozachenko-Leonenko k-NN entropy with k = 4 on per-method standardised velocities at an equal sample size n = 150. (b) Grid coverage with 4 equal bins per dimension between the pooled 1st and 99th percentiles, 4^15 (about 1.1e9) cells, counted cumulatively. HUMAN-LIKENESS (p.7 section 2.9): cycles are aligned at right initial contact (model segmented at the rising edge of the right vertical GRF) and time-normalised to 101 points. Pearson r is computed between model and human mean waveforms. Kinematics and vGRF are compared with Fukuchi et al. 2017 (PeerJ 5:e3298) treadmill running at 2.5, 3.5 and 4.5 m/s, grouping model cycles by mean centre-of-mass speed within +/-0.35 m/s. EMG uses Van Hooren and Meijer 2024 (Data in Brief 54:110312), 19 participants at 5.0 m/s, filtered 20-450 Hz band-pass, rectified and 10 Hz low-pass, then peak-normalised; it is compared with model activations from cycles of mean speed >= 4.3 m/s (129 cycles, Fig. 6). HARDWARE: 'a single NVIDIA RTX 5070 GPU with a 24-thread Intel Core Ultra 9 CPU' (p.8). No head-to-head wall-clock comparison is reported. KINESIS. Train on the 946 KIT-Locomotion clips and evaluate on the 108 unseen test clips. Metrics (p.5): frame coverage (% of dataset frames imitated), success (tracked markers within 0.5 m of the reference on average over the trial) and global MPJPE in mm, as mean and SEM over N = 3 evaluation runs (Table I p.4). Downstream (pp.5-6): text-to-control with MDM motions, judged qualitatively. Target reaching uses a 2x2 m area, 5 s (150 frames) per episode, termination at root height < 0.7 m, success within 0.1 m and 1000 random trials; it is fine-tuned from expert 2 for 5,000-10,000 more epochs, and the from-scratch baseline gets 5,000 epochs (App. p.9). The Legs+Back penalty kick is tested against 3 goalkeeper strategies. EMG (p.6-7): gait-averaged correlations with the Wang et al. 2023 and Scherpereel et al. 2023 datasets, compared against DynSyn and DEP-RL on the Legs model, plus MPJAE over 4 left-leg joints (Fig. 6).

ablations_that_matter.ablation: Excitation-hold vs Plain SAC (holding without lambda)
ablations_that_matter.result: Holding alone lifts return by about an order of magnitude on the simulation-step axis.
ablations_that_matter.caveat: Confounded with discount horizon: gamma 0.99 per transition gives Excitation-hold ~10 s and Plain SAC ~1 s (computed here).

ablations_that_matter.ablation: Lambda-hold vs Excitation-hold (control variable at equal decision points)
ablations_that_matter.result: Lambda-hold return is more than an order of magnitude higher. The authors attribute 'the larger part of the advantage' to lambda plus the reflex law rather than to holding.
ablations_that_matter.caveat: This is the paper's cleanest comparison (matched decision points and horizon), but it has only 2 seeds, and exp(v) returns compress to about a 2.3 m/s mean-speed gap per decade.

ablations_that_matter.ablation: Synergy (fixed NMF basis from lambda-hold's own best rollouts) vs lambda-hold
ablations_that_matter.result: Synergy stalls at rudimentary locomotion, with the lowest coverage and entropy that is higher than Plain SAC. This supports the claim that lambda's state-dependent coordination beats a fixed basis.
ablations_that_matter.caveat: The Synergy baseline has a 1 s horizon (no hold) and omits the mirroring used by its original study.

ablations_that_matter.ablation: DEP-RL (DEP+MPO, prior implementation, rescaled to 0.01 s)
ablations_that_matter.result: Best baseline late in training: about 2.6 m/s with a non-human-like gait. Coverage is ~2.5x lower than lambda-hold.
ablations_that_matter.caveat: Hyper-parameters come from the author's H2190 running config (they match the sconegym/DEP-RL sconerun_h2190 YAML), and DEP-RL was trained under a reward it was not tuned for.

ablations_that_matter.ablation: RSI from a self-generated archive (App. B.1)
ablations_that_matter.result: The late-training oscillation, in which the fast sprint is lost and relearned, disappears; return becomes smooth at ~1e5 (figure-read). Top speed stays near 4.7 m/s.
ablations_that_matter.caveat: The fraction of RSI resets and the archive size are not reported. RSI is allowed under our gate because it changes neither reward nor body.

ablations_that_matter.ablation: vmax curriculum 10 -> 20 L_opt/s (on top of RSI)
ablations_that_matter.result: Top speed ~6.5 m/s, which identifies the H2190 force-velocity relation as the ceiling.
ablations_that_matter.caveat: Explicitly diagnostic, and forbidden by our gate. The schedule end lies beyond the plotted budget.

ablations_that_matter.caveat: Cheap to run in a reimplementation; it separates reflex-law benefits from temporal abstraction.

Lambda-Hold: the muscle strength scenario is undisclosed. The only public H2190 running scenario (sconegym db2d2c1 data-v1/H2190_run.scone) sets muscle_force_multiplier = 2 with a 0.005 s fixed control step; the walking scenario H2190.scone does not. The paper's DEP-RL hyper-parameters (1024-unit MLP, actor lr 3.53e-5, critic 6.08e-5, dual 2.13e-3, 0.025 s original step) match the author YAML for sconerun_h2190-v1 exactly (KB sconerun-h2190-config.yaml). The termination thresholds (0.5 m COM, 0.9 m head) and 0.01 s step also equal sconegym defaults (gaitgym.py). A doubled-strength plant therefore cannot be excluded. This is inference, not proof.

Lambda-Hold: the reflex has zero delay and G_tonic = 50 saturates excitation 0.02 L_opt above threshold. It is essentially a stiff, delay-free length servo, whereas real stretch reflexes have 30-50 ms latencies and much lower gains. 'Physiologically grounded' rests on the form of the law only. SCONE's own neural_delays_FEA_v4.zml (hip 10 ms, knee 20 ms, ankle 40 ms) is not mentioned.

Lambda-Hold: a horizon confound in the baseline comparison. With gamma = 0.99 per transition, Plain SAC and Synergy (0.01 s decisions) have a ~1 s effective horizon against ~10 s for the hold methods. Only DEP-RL was rescaled. Part of the Excitation-hold vs Plain SAC gap may be horizon rather than intermittency.

Lambda-Hold: 'orders of magnitude faster' (section 3.1 title) is read off log-scale returns of an exp(v) reward. One decade of return equals about 2.3 m/s of mean speed at equal episode length, so the plots overstate the performance gap as a learning-speed ratio.

reproduction_relevance: Lambda-Hold is the only published muscle-driven RL result that clears our replication gate's speed on its own plant (4.0 m/s in ~1 h, top ~4.7 m/s), and it does so with the minimal reward our gate freezes. It is also the Phase-2 starting design. It cannot be reproduced as published: the code is TBA, SCONE/Hyfydy leaves the lab after 2026-09-25, only 2 seeds are shown, and the strength multiplier is undisclosed. Any MuJoCo version is therefore an independent reimplementation on a different plant. MyoLeg-80 differs from H2190 in ways that cut both ways. (1) Its leg muscles total 1.5x H2190's F0 at multiplier 1. (2) MuJoCo's quadratic force-velocity curve gives 1.4-1.5x more force than a Hill hyperbola at 2-3 L0/s shortening, which is exactly where the paper locates its 4.7 m/s ceiling. (3) Its active F-L curves are very wide (median lmax 3.5). (4) It has rigid tendons with no elastic recoil. (5) It has no lumbar DOF or trunk muscles, but it does have mtp toes. (6) Its contact model differs. (7) Its activations match EMG worse: Beyond Kinematics reports r 0.11 for MuJoCo vs 0.40 for HyFyDy. Items 1-3 favour reaching >= 4.0 m/s without strength or vmax changes; items 4-7 threaten realism and stability. Porting the lambda law also needs a normalisation audit. MyoLeg's normalised lengths are MTU-derived, 26 muscles have clamped ranges, and glmax3 would sit permanently saturated under the published bounds. Kinesis supplies the open MyoLeg-80 MJCF with pinned parameters, a working MuJoCo length-target muscle controller (the PD mode, a close cousin of lambda-control) and pretrained locomotion priors. It does not supply a sprint-capable human: its checkpoints are reference-conditioned imitation or target-reach policies trained on walking-dominated KIT data whose 90 short 'run' clips have unreported speed, and imitation needs SMPL plus AMASS licences. For SMAT staging, three points follow. (a) A lambda-hold human is an SMDP SAC agent acting 8 times per stride, whereas SMAT's exo actor is 50 Hz PPO with a shared critic; staging must either freeze the SAC human (stage 3) or define a joint SMDP update (stage 4). (b) GRF events are also natural exo triggers, since Moon et al.'s sprint suit is gait-event-timed. (c) The exo observations must exclude lambda, l and v, which a real device cannot sense. The paper's missing 'lambda without hold' and fixed-interval-hold arms map onto our matrix conditions G and H (06-architecture note).
reimplementation_recipe: 0. Label and pre-register. Call it 'independent MuJoCo/MyoLeg reimplementation of Lambda-Hold (arXiv 2608.17030v1)'. Before any run, freeze the gate metric: per seed, the maximum over complete right-foot gait cycles of per-cycle mean COM forward speed, from 10 deterministic 20 s episodes started from standing, using the last checkpoint. PASS if the median over 5 seeds is >= 4.0 m/s. Also report the best 1 s window speed and the fall rate. Forbidden in gate runs: any change to F0, vmax, fvmax, F-L curves, mass, the Eq. 2 reward, or the vmax curriculum.

1. Model. Use MyoLeg-80 'Legs' from amathislab/Kinesis@cddab3c data/xml/legs/myolegs.xml + myolegs_assets.xml, which needs no SMPL for the model itself, or the matching MyoSuite myo_sim myolegs; record the file sha256 either way. Keep all actuator parameters: vmax 10, fvmax 1.4, dynprm (0.01, 0.04), per-muscle F0 summing to 92,428 N. Compile once and record total mass, inertia, nq/nv/nu = 80 and the joint list. Note in the report that it has no arms (like H2190) and no lumbar DOF or trunk muscles (unlike H2190), so the action dimension is 80, not 90.

2. Physics. Use native MuJoCo on CPU. Set opt.timestep = 0.002 s (verify against 0.001 s on a 2 s rollout) and keep the XML contact and solver settings. The lambda-law/controller step is 0.01 s, i.e. 5 substeps, matching the paper's 0.01 s step. Do not use Kinesis's 1/150 s for sprint impacts without a parity check.

3. Muscle state, vectorised over 80 actuators, using MuJoCo's own normalisation (engine_util_misc.c mju_muscleGain): L0 = (lr1 - lr0)/(range1 - range0) from model.actuator_lengthrange and actuator_gainprm[:,0:2]; l = range0 + (data.actuator_length - lr0)/L0; v = data.actuator_velocity/L0 in L0/s, with positive meaning lengthening, the same sign convention as the paper's rectified phasic term. Unit test: recompute FL*FV from (l, v) with MuJoCo's formulas and check that it reproduces (data.actuator_force - mju_muscleBias(...))/(-F0*act) to 1e-6. The bias term is the passive force.
4. Recruitment law exactly as Eq. 1: e = clip(50*(l - lambda) + 0.1*max(v, 0), 0, 1), written to data.ctrl once per 0.01 s. Use zero delay, as the paper implies. Keep e for logging only.

5. Lambda-range pre-flight audit (blocking). Log each muscle's l range over (i) its lengthrange, (ii) the standing keyframe and (iii) a kinematic playback of a running clip if available. Expected from the ledger: glmax3_r/l have l >= 1.367 everywhere (LT = -0.26 m), so under lambda <= 1.2 they are permanently fully excited. 26 muscles have clamped range ends with inflated L0. Primary arm: the published bounds [0.6, 1.2] for all muscles. Pre-declared fallback arm (a controller-side deviation that leaves the body unchanged): raise the upper lambda bound only for muscles whose l cannot fall below 1.2 (glmax3) to range0 + 0.05. Report both arms if the fallback is used.

6. GRF events. Every 0.01 s, compute per-foot vertical GRF as the world-z component of the mj_contactForce normals summed over contacts between the floor and that foot's bodies (calcn, talus, toes). Threshold 0.05 x BW, where BW = compiled total mass x 9.81. Contact state = GRF > threshold. Events are rising edges (strike) and falling edges (toe-off) of either foot.

7. Decision scheduler, a per-env state machine on the 0.01 s grid. Keep the last three event times. The candidate next decision is the earlier of the next event and the sub-point t_e1 + 0.5*(t_e2 - t_e3), where t_e1 is the most recent event and t_e2, t_e3 the second- and third-most recent. Enforce a minimum hold of 0.05 s (an event inside it defers the decision to t_dec + 0.05: assumption A1) and a maximum of 0.15 s (forced decision: A2). With fewer than 3 events (standing start) use events plus the 0.15 s cap only (A3). Unit-test on a synthetic running GRF trace: expect 8 decisions per stride, as in Fig. 2.

8. Observation (all per 0.01 s state at decision time). l (80), v (80), actuator_force/F0 (80; normalisation A4), held lambda (80); independent joint angles and velocities (root orientation plus hip x3, knee, ankle, subtalar and mtp per side; no root x/y position; coupled knee/patella DOFs omitted); per-foot contact flag (2) and GRF/BW 3-vector (6); vestibular = torso/head orientation quaternion (4) + angular velocity (3). This is about 360-380 dims, not 432, because of the 80 muscles and different DOFs. Wrap in VecNormalize (observations and rewards, running mean/var) as in Table 1. Exclude excitations and activations.
9. Action. 80-dim SAC tanh output a in [-1,1] -> lambda = 0.9 + 0.3*a (linear map: A5).

10. Reward, unchanged. Per 0.01 s step r = exp(v_x)*exp(-(v_lat/0.1)^2), with COM velocity from mujoco.mj_subtreeVel then data.subtree_linvel[root] (or mass-weighted cvel). First identify the model's forward axis (the Kinesis directional task places its default goal at -1.265 m along x). SMDP transition reward = sum over the hold. gamma = 0.99 per decision (A6, per Table 1).

11. Termination and horizon. Terminate if COM z < 0.5 m or head z < 0.9 m (the head is a fixed body in the rigid torso). Training time limit 10 s (A7, consistent with sconegym's 1000-step default and the Fig. 3/7 return magnitudes). Treat truncation as time-limit, not terminal. Reset to the standing keyframe with small noise (A8: joint position sigma 0.05 rad, velocity sigma 0.1 rad/s, as in sconegym).

12. SAC per Table 1. SB3 SAC('MlpPolicy', use_sde=True, sde_sample_freq=4, learning_rate=3e-4, gamma=0.99, tau=0.005, batch_size=256, buffer_size=500_000, train_freq=1, gradient_steps=2, ent_coef='auto', policy_kwargs=dict(net_arch=[256,256])) on 24 SubprocVecEnv envs, where one env step equals one hold. Unspecified choices take SB3 defaults and are logged (A9): learning_starts, activation, log_std_init, target entropy.

13. Budget: 150e6 simulation steps (about 15e6 decisions) per seed. Evaluate every 5e6 simulation steps with deterministic actions. Log speed, fall rate, decisions per stride and wall-clock. Early smoke check: per the paper, H2190 reached about 4.0 m/s in about an hour. If MyoLeg is below 2 m/s after 30e6 simulation steps, stop and debug normalisation and scheduler before spending seeds.

14. Optional RSI (App. B.1) as a separately named arm 'lambda-hold+RSI'. After 3e6 decisions, draw a fraction p of resets from an archive of states taken from the top-K return episodes (A10: p = 0.5, K = 20 episodes, states sampled uniformly from their second half). The gate permits it because it changes neither body nor reward. Never enable the vmax curriculum in gate runs.
15. Gate run: 5 seeds x 150e6 simulation steps, then the frozen evaluation from step 0. Report the per-seed maxima, the median, and a bootstrap CI over seeds.

16. Fidelity checks from the paper's section 2.9, on cycles grouped by per-cycle mean COM speed within +/-0.35 m/s. Sagittal hip/knee/ankle + vGRF against Fukuchi et al. 2017 at 2.5/3.5/4.5 m/s. EMG against Van Hooren and Meijer 2024 at 5.0 m/s for the MyoLeg analogues of the 11 muscles (soleus, gasmed, gaslat, tibant, vasmed, vaslat, recfem, bflh, semiten, glmax1-3 pooled, glmed1-3 pooled), with 20-450 Hz band-pass, rectification, 10 Hz low-pass and peak normalisation. Compare with the paper's r values.

17. Plant diagnostics: replicate Fig. 8 for iliacus, psoas and recfem (activation, normalised velocity, FV factor (1+V)^2, force/F0 at activation > 0.9). This shows whether MyoLeg's ceiling is force-velocity-limited like H2190 or limited elsewhere (rigid tendon, contact, balance).

18. Matched-budget controls (these become matrix arms). Plain SAC on 80 excitations at 0.01 s; the same with horizon-matched gamma = 0.99^(1/10) per step; Excitation-hold at the same decision points; lambda every 0.01 s with no hold (missing in the paper); lambda with fixed 0.08 s holds (the paper's untested claim).

19. Throughput before scaling. Measure mj_step for MyoLeg-80 at 2 ms on one EPYC core first (not measured yet; the 26-muscle myolegs26+Hippo costs 62.7 us per step on an EPYC 9535 per myoassist_framework.json). Size concurrent seeds so that envs across concurrent seeds stay within about 60 cores and replay buffers plus env processes fit in 30 GB (see throughput_notes).
20. Only after the gate passes, run separate 200 m evaluation episodes of at least 50 s to test stability beyond the ~10 s training horizon. Train on 200 m only as a new, labelled condition.

throughput_notes: Lambda-Hold (reported). About 4.0 m/s emerges in about 1 h on an RTX 5070 + 24-thread Core Ultra 9 with Hyfydy (CPU physics), SB3 SAC and 24 envs (p.8; Table 1). Curves run to about 150e6 simulation steps (about 15e6 decisions) per seed; wall-clock for the full run is not reported. Because each hold is one transition, the learner sees about 10x fewer transitions than simulation steps, so the policy-update cost is small and CPU physics dominates. Kinesis (reported). 1 A100 + 128 CPU threads, 128 envs, 51,200 samples per epoch at 30 Hz control and 150 Hz physics; total training time not reported. MuscleMimic says Kinesis needs about 10 days on 128 CPU envs + A100 for the 290-actuator model (MuscleMimic p.3). Our server (estimates, ARGUED, to be measured). MyoLeg-80 mj_step cost at 2 ms is unmeasured; the 26-muscle myolegs26+Hippo costs 62.7 us per step on an EPYC 9535 core. If MyoLeg-80 costs 100-200 us per step, one 0.01 s lambda step (5 substeps) is 0.5-1 ms, and 150e6 simulation steps is about 21-42 core-hours of physics per seed, i.e. under an hour of physics at 48 cores if parallelised. With 24 envs per seed (the paper's setting) a seed is learner-bound, not physics-bound: 15e6 decisions / 24 envs x 2 gradient steps is about 1.25e6 SAC updates of batch 256 on 2x256 MLPs, likely 1-3 h on the RTX 5090 (an unmeasured assumption). RAM: a float32 replay of 5e5 x (2 x ~370 obs + 80 act) is about 1.6 GB per seed, and 24 MuJoCo subprocesses are roughly 1-2.5 GB, so 2-3 concurrent seeds fit in 30 GB with headroom (a 5-seed gate is then about 2 batches). GPU physics (MJX-Warp) is not needed for the published SAC design. It would pay off for sweeps over the lambda bounds and scheduler assumptions. The lambda law is elementwise and ports trivially, but the per-env GRF-event scheduler needs a vectorised state machine, and variable-length holds complicate fixed-step GPU batching unless every env is stepped every 0.01 s with masked policy queries.
rival_explanations: Stiff length servo rather than EP physiology: with G_tonic = 50 and no delay, each muscle is almost a bang-bang switch at lambda that holds joint configurations stiffly. Any held length-target controller could provide the same stability and effective action compression, e.g. Kinesis's PD target-length mode or joint-space PD targets. The paper never compares against one.

Temporal abstraction and horizon: holds put decisions about 0.1 s apart. With gamma = 0.99 per decision that is a ~10 s horizon, against ~1 s for the per-step SAC baselines. Credit assignment over a sprint's acceleration phase may explain much of the gap between hold methods and Plain SAC/Synergy, independent of lambda.

Plant strength: if the H2190 run scenario's muscle_force_multiplier = 2 was in effect, both 'sprint emerges' and '4.7 m/s' reflect a doubled-strength body. The F-V ceiling analysis would then describe an unrealistically strong model.

Reward shape and log-plot reading: exp(v) makes return exponential in speed, so large return ratios correspond to modest speed differences, and 'orders of magnitude faster learning' partly restates a different speed level.

Human-likeness from plant and speed, not controller: kinematic shape correlations (r 0.83-0.97) may mostly come from musculoskeletal geometry and running at speed (any running gait has similar sagittal shapes). No baseline reached comparable speed for a controlled comparison.

Kinesis EMG advantage from imitation constraints: better EMG correlation than DEP-RL/DynSyn may come from tracking human kinematics (which constrains activation timing) rather than muscle-level plausibility. The authors test this only partially via MPJAE, and MuscleMimic reports that 'strong kinematic imitation does not automatically guarantee physiologically faithful muscle activations' (MuscleMimic arXiv 2603.25544 p.10).
ideas_sparked: Plant-fidelity axis as a finding: run the identical lambda-hold port on MyoLeg with MuJoCo's native quadratic F-V and with a Hill-hyperbolic F-V (via a CPU gain callback or a custom actuator). If the MuJoCo curve alone moves the speed ceiling past 4.7 m/s, that quantifies how much 'sprint capability' is a muscle-model artefact. This is relevant to the Exo-Plore and Beyond Kinematics caveats in the brief.

Event-synchronous exosuit: query the hip-exo actor at the same 8 GRF-event decision points per stride, with a small per-hold torque-profile parameterisation (e.g. peak time and magnitude within the hold). This mirrors gait-event-timed sprint suits (Moon et al.) and shrinks exo exploration exactly as holds shrink human exploration.

Complete the 2x2 factorial the paper left open (lambda vs excitation x hold vs no-hold) plus fixed-interval holds, all at matched gamma-horizon. This is cheap, it maps onto matrix arms G/H, and it would be publishable as a clarification of Lambda-Hold.

Use Kinesis's PD target-length code (target_length_to_force + force_to_activation) as a ready MuJoCo implementation of the rival 'length servo' control law. Hold it on the same GRF events for a controller-form ablation (reflex excitation law vs force-inversion law).

Muscle-normalisation audit as a test: a unit test that flags any muscle whose l range cannot cross the lambda bounds (glmax3 today) or whose L0 deviates from the OpenSim lopt by more than 20% (26 clamped muscles). It prevents silent saturation in both lambda and exo experiments.

Strength-matched cross-check: if a Hyfydy licence becomes available again, H2190 at muscle_force_multiplier 1 vs 2 under lambda-hold directly measures how much the published speed depends on strength. Record this as an open question for the authors (e.g. an email asking which scenario was used).

Long-horizon sprint: the published objective has a ~10 s effective horizon. For 200 m, add a separately labelled condition with longer episodes and gamma per unit time. A fatigue model (MyoSuite 3CC-r, present in Kinesis but uncalibrated for sprint) could come later as its own condition, so that assistance effects on late-race deceleration become testable.
